item.title: Safe and Trustworthy Autonomous Systems in Real-World Environments
item.content:encoded:
Heye Huang, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Inhi Kim, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Boqi Li, Beihang University

Haotian Shi, Tongji University

Lei Yang, Nanyang Technological University

Kailai Sun, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

Autonomous systems operating in complex real-world environments face significant challenges in ensuring safety, reliability, and generalization. This special issue seeks research that advances trustworthy autonomy through integration of data-driven learning with structured knowledge, world models, formal verification, and uncertainty reasoning. Contributions should address both average-case and long-tail safety-critical scenarios, with emphasis on how autonomous systems can identify risks, adapt continually, and coordinate with other agents.

The scope includes autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, and other safety-critical platforms. Submissions may combine learning, optimization, control, simulation, and human-centered methods provided they clearly contribute to trustworthy autonomous behavior. The issue welcomes original research, reviews, benchmarks, and perspective articles demonstrating methodological novelty, rigorous evaluation, or insights transferable to real-world autonomous system deployment.

Appel publié par Expert Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Trustworthy Content Governance and Safe Generative AI in the Age of Large Language Models
item.content:encoded:
This special issue addresses the challenges of governing content and ensuring safety in generative AI systems, particularly as large language models become increasingly prevalent. The issue seeks research on establishing trustworthy frameworks and mechanisms for managing content while developing safer generative AI technologies.

Appel publié par Information Processing & Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Timeline

item.title: Mathematical Foundations for Trustworthy AI Applications in Transportation Systems
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on the mathematical and theoretical underpinnings necessary to develop trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for transportation applications. The collection seeks work that bridges mathematical rigor with practical AI implementation in transportation contexts, addressing critical concerns about safety, reliability, and transparency in automated decision-making systems.

Contributions are invited from researchers working on formal verification methods, explainable AI techniques, robustness analysis, and uncertainty quantification as they apply to transportation challenges. The special issue aims to advance our understanding of how to build AI systems that can be trusted by both technical experts and end-users in real-world transportation scenarios.

Appel publié par Transportation Research Part B Methodological. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Trustworthy AI in transportation
  • Mathematical foundations of AI
  • Transportation systems
  • AI safety and reliability
  • Verification and validation of AI models
  • Explainability and interpretability
  • Robustness and adversarial resilience
  • Uncertainty quantification
  • Real-time decision-making systems

Timeline

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline
